scheme_name: PMMSY: Inputs for fresh water Aquaculture including Composite fish culture, Scampi, Pangasius, Tilapia etc - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

The primary objective of PMMSY is to enhance fish production and productivity in the country. 

The scheme aims to achieve an increase in fish production to 22 million metric tons by the year 2024-2025. 

This initiative is also focused on promoting sustainable and responsible aquaculture practices. 

The PMMSY is designed to provide financial assistance to fish farmers and aquaculture entrepreneurs. 

The scheme specifically targets various forms of aquaculture including composite fish culture, scampi farming, pangasius cultivation, and tilapia farming. 

In Haryana, the PMMSY aims to boost the state's aquaculture sector significantly. 

The scheme provides financial assistance of up to 60% of the project cost for individual farmers. 

For groups of farmers or cooperatives, the financial assistance can go up to 80% of the project cost. 

The maximum project cost eligible for assistance is capped at INR 20 lakh for individual farmers. 

For groups or cooperatives, the maximum project cost eligible for assistance is INR 50 lakh. 

The scheme also includes provisions for the establishment of hatcheries, feed mills, and other necessary infrastructure. 

Eligible beneficiaries must be at least 18 years of age. 

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants. 

The income criteria for eligibility is that the applicant should belong to a family with an annual income of less than INR 8 lakh. 

Educational qualifications are not explicitly mentioned as a requirement for this scheme. 

The application process for PMMSY in Haryana involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must approach the local fisheries department or the district fisheries officer. 

The applicant is required to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the fisheries department office. 

Along with the application form, the applicant must submit a project report detailing the proposed aquaculture activities. 

The project report should include information such as the type of fish to be cultured, the area of land to be used, and the estimated costs involved. 

Documents required for the application include identity proof, address proof, and income certificate. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the district fisheries officer. 

If the application meets all the criteria, it will be forwarded to the state fisheries department for approval. 

The state fisheries department will then conduct a field verification of the proposed site. 

After verification, the project will be sanctioned, and the financial assistance will be disbursed. 

The disbursement of funds is typically done in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The first installment is usually released after the project is sanctioned. 

Subsequent installments are released upon the completion of specific milestones as outlined in the project report. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the need for training and capacity building of fish farmers. 

The scheme includes provisions for skill development programs to enhance the knowledge and skills of farmers. 

The training programs cover various aspects of aquaculture including best practices in fish farming, disease management, and feed management. 

The implementing authority for PMMSY in Haryana is the Department of Fisheries, Haryana. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries can be found on the official Haryana government website. 

The PMMSY also aims to promote the use of technology in aquaculture. 

This includes the adoption of modern techniques such as biofloc technology and recirculatory aquaculture systems. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of fish markets and value-added processing units. 

This is aimed at increasing the income of fish farmers and improving the overall value chain of fish production. 

The PMMSY is expected to create significant employment opportunities in the aquaculture sector. 

It is estimated that the scheme will generate around 15 lakh direct and indirect jobs by 2025. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the nutritional security of the population by increasing fish availability. 

Fish is a rich source of protein and essential nutrients. 

The PMMSY aligns with the National Fisheries Policy which aims to promote sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to boost the blue economy in India. 

The blue economy encompasses the sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth, improved livelihoods, and jobs. 

The PMMSY is funded through the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB). 

The NFDB is responsible for implementing various fisheries development programs across the country. 

The PMMSY also focuses on the conservation of aquatic resources. 

This includes measures to protect fish breeding grounds and promote biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems. 

The scheme encourages the participation of women and marginalized communities in aquaculture. 

Special provisions are made to support women fish farmers through targeted training and financial assistance. 

The PMMSY is expected to contribute significantly to the overall economic development of Haryana. 

By enhancing fish production, the scheme aims to improve the livelihoods of thousands of fish farmers in the state. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of research and development in aquaculture. 

This includes collaboration with research institutions to develop improved fish breeds and farming techniques. 

The scheme is a significant step towards achieving self-sufficiency in fish production in India. 

It aims to reduce the dependency on fish imports and promote domestic fish consumption. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive initiative that addresses various aspects of aquaculture development. 

From financial assistance to skill development, the scheme provides a holistic approach to enhancing the fisheries sector in Haryana. 

The PMMSY is a crucial component of the government's efforts to promote sustainable agriculture and rural development. 

Overall, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana represents a significant investment in the future of aquaculture in India. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable aquaculture sector that can benefit millions of people across the country.
